about.title: Wildomar Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Wildomar sits along busy Riverside County corridors where local traffic and commuters heading toward I-15 often collide with pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers. Public crash records show dozens of injury collisions each year here, with Thursday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. showing up repeatedly as a high-frequency window on roads like Palomar Street and Clinton Keith Road. After a wreck, medical bills and insurance calls can pile up fast, and it's easy to feel unsure of your next step. We handle car accident claims and can review the details of what happened. Our team can help you understand your options, deal with the insurance company, and work toward fair compensation for your losses, all on a contingency basis so you owe nothing unless you recover.

items.title: Time Limits Matter
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a car accident lawsuit, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity's road or vehicle was involved. We can help you figure out which deadline applies before it's too late.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the crash. Your compensation is simply reduced by your percentage of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to have your case reviewed. You only pay if we secure a recovery on your behalf.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with us. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim, and we can help protect what you say. Preserving evidence and being careful with early statements can make a real difference later.

items.question: What if my accident happened at a Wildomar intersection with a lot of reported crashes, like near Clinton Keith Road?
items.answer: Public crash-count data simply reflects how much traffic and reported activity a corridor sees, not fault or blame for any individual collision. What matters most for your claim is the specific facts of your crash — how it happened, who was involved, and the evidence available. We can help gather police reports, witness accounts, and any available footage tied to your location.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Wildomar car accident?
items.answer: In most California car accident cases you have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If a government vehicle or roadway defect was involved, that deadline can shrink to as little as six months, so it's important to act promptly. We can confirm which timeline applies to your specific situation.
